author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory — the page and the machine-readable list — can be narrowed to a single specialty, named in full and case-insensitively. Neither form gains a control for choosing one; the specialty is named in the request and carried forward by paging links.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is asked for that specialty, then only those veterinarians are listed
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable directory is asked for that specialty, then only those veterinarians are carried
given a specialty written in different letter case from the stored name, when either form is asked for it, then it matches
given only part of a stored specialty name, when either form is asked for it, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is asked for it, then the response succeeds and carries no veterinarian
given an empty or spaces-only specialty, when either form is asked for it, then it behaves as though no specialty were named
given surrounding spaces around a named specialty, when either form is asked for it, then the result matches the same name without them
given more matching veterinarians than fit one page, when the page is asked for that specialty, then paging runs over the matching veterinarians alone
given a page narrowed to a specialty, when a link to a further page is followed, then that page is narrowed to the same specialty
given no specialty is named, when either form is requested, then every veterinarian is listed as before
given either form, when it is rendered, then no form, dropdown, or other control for choosing a specialty is present
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface
narrowing the directory to more than one specialty at once
free-text veterinarian search, which NG-9 still declines
matching on part of a specialty name
notes: The owner fixed the address contract and it is a product decision, not a design choice: /vets.html?specialty=<name> for the page and /vets?specialty=<name> for the machine-readable form. Record it in system-design.md#contracts — the PRD keeps addresses out by existing convention. REQ-VET-003 (the machine-readable directory as a supported surface) is newly stated and is met by today's behavior; this slice's unfiltered assertions cover its Done-when bullet. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its ID is not reused. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-30-non-goal-vet-search-narrowed.md; that file is outside the product-requirements-expert write scope. Three open questions were recorded rather than decided: multiple specialties per request, a visible control, and whether a specialty is named as stored or as translated. Each took the narrowest reading.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds no layer: a derived repository finder, a request parameter on each of the two existing handlers, and a model attribute the paging links carry. It fits the feature-package shape (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization) and the derived-query pattern OwnerRepository already uses. One piece is genuinely new ground and is recorded rather than left implicit: the vet cache's keys are a closed set today, and a caller-supplied specialty would make them unbounded against a cache with no eviction. ADR 2026-08-30-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads decides that the filtered reads carry no @Cacheable. The URL contract the owner fixed is now recorded in system-design.md as Contracts > Veterinarian directory addresses, since the PRD records no addresses. NG-9 no longer bars the slice (ADR 2026-08-30-non-goal-vet-search-narrowed), and its index row is now in docs/adr/README.md.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a specialty-filtered finder pair mirroring the existing findAll()/findAll(Pageable) overloads: one Collection-returning for /vets, one Page-returning for /vets.html. Keep @Transactional(readOnly = true); add no @Cacheable.
VetController.showVetList and VetController.showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty request parameter; a null or blank-after-strip value routes to the existing unfiltered call unchanged.
VetController.addPaginationModel adds the normalized specialty (or null) to the model so vetList.html can carry it in every paging link.
vets/vetList.html paging links carry the specialty; no form, input, or dropdown is added to the page.
No change to Vets, Vet, Specialty, CacheConfiguration, or the schema and seed scripts.

patterns.description: derived paged finder on a Spring Data repository interface — the shape the specialty finder follows; use the explicit property path findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase so the traversal into Specialty.name is unambiguous, and IgnoreCase so matching is whole-name and case-insensitive

blank-parameter normalization: strip the value, treat empty as the unfiltered case. Mirror this inline form rather than introducing an @InitBinder StringTrimmerEditor — VetController binds no complex type today, and a new binder would owe the identifier disallow list that security-principles.md requires of every binder

the existing paging links use the preprocessed string form @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}, which does not URL-encode. Links carrying the specialty use the parameterized link expression instead — @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} — which URL-encodes the value and omits a null parameter, so the unfiltered page renders the links it renders today

risks.risk: Caching the filtered read would key cache entries on caller-supplied text, in a cache with no eviction configured — unbounded memory growth from a query parameter
risks.mitigation: the filtered finders carry no @Cacheable; decided in docs/adr/2026-08-30-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md and stated in the VetRepository row of system-design.md Contracts

risks.risk: A specialty value interpolated into a paging href through the template's existing string-preprocessing form would not be URL-encoded, letting a crafted value smuggle further query parameters into the link
risks.mitigation: use Thymeleaf's parameterized link expression for every link that carries the specialty; Thymeleaf's attribute escaping stays on and covers the HTML layer

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is an EAGER @ManyToMany, so the filtered query joins a collection; a mismatch between the count query and the page content would break paging
risks.mitigation: use the Distinct keyword in the finder. A vet holds a given specialty at most once (Set-valued association), so duplicates are not expected — assert page totals in theVetListShouldPageOverTheMatchingVeterinariansAlone rather than assuming

risks.risk: Owner search matches case-insensitively by column collation, which diverges under PostgreSQL (Known Defects)
risks.mitigation: specialty matching uses IgnoreCase in the query, so it is vendor-independent; do not add a collation-dependent column or index for this

risks.risk: architecture-principles.md holds that a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing deviation
risks.mitigation: stripping and blank-as-absent are input normalization at the trust boundary, which the Web controller row admits as binding the request. No matching, paging, or filtering decision beyond that belongs in VetController — the predicate lives in the derived query

notes: Narrow readings taken where the contract left room, per the dispatch's binding instruction. (1) Parameter name is exactly 'specialty' on both surfaces, per the owner's fixed contract. (2) One specialty per request; a repeated parameter is not a designed case — Spring binds the first value to a String parameter, and no requirement covers a second. (3) The specialty is named as stored, never translated; Specialty names are data, and no message-bundle key is added. (4) Blank means absent on both surfaces, and the machine-readable form behaves the same as the page. (5) No control is added to either surface; the model attribute exists only so the paging links can carry the value. Durable memory written this dispatch: system-design.md gains Contracts > Veterinarian directory addresses and a persistence sentence on vendor-independent matching; the Vets, VetRepository, and VetController Implements cells now cite REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004; the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable route serves no requirement is retired, since REQ-VET-003 now states that surface; Open Question 5 notes that the filtered reads stay outside the cache. docs/adr/README.md gains index rows for the non-goal ADR the product-requirements-expert wrote and for the new caching ADR. No design-doc-autofix records were present, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge. doctor.py check reports only the pre-existing, unrelated project-data spec_version failure.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: VetRepository adds only derived finders (findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase, with and without Pageable). No @Query, no EntityManager.createQuery, no string-concatenated JPQL/SQL anywhere in the diff; the caller-supplied specialty reaches the database as a bound parameter. IgnoreCase is realized by the derived-query mechanism, not by concatenated SQL functions.

Reflected XSS / parameter smuggling in paging links: all five link families in vets/vetList.html (numbered sequence, first, previous, next, last) use the parameterized link expression @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} with a null branch that omits the parameter. None uses the pre-existing string-preprocessing form @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}, which does not URL-encode. Grep across src/main/resources/templates confirms no remaining __${...}__ preprocessing and no th:utext; Thymeleaf's default attribute escaping stays on. The regression test asserts specialty=radiology&page=99 renders as specialty=radiology%26page%3D99 and never as the unencoded form, so neither parameter smuggling nor markup breakout of the href is reachable.

Cache as a resource boundary: @Cacheable("vets") appears only on the two unfiltered findAll overloads; both specialty-filtered finders carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) alone. Annotation placement matches the intent recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-30-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md - no caller-supplied text becomes a key in an unevicted cache. The uncached filtered path is a read-only, parameterized, page-limited query (page size 5) against an indexed join, so it opens no new resource boundary beyond the already-open unauthenticated read surface described in system-design.md Security Context.

Mass assignment: VetController binds only simple request parameters (int page, String specialty) and no complex command object, so the security-principles.md rule that every request-bound *type* disallow identifier binding is not engaged. Omitting @InitBinder is correct here - adding an empty or partial binder would have been the weaker choice, since the project's disallow list ("id", "*.id") has nothing to apply to. Blank normalization via strip() in namedSpecialtyOrNull is a pure value normalization on the way in, not a security control being substituted for one.

Failure and disclosure behavior: a no-match specialty flows through the derived finder to an empty Page, rendering HTTP 200 with an empty table - no exception, no error page, and nothing distinguishing 'unknown specialty' from 'specialty with no vets', so the endpoint leaks no information about which specialty names exist. The specialty value never reaches an exception message, a log line, or the error page. Unbounded specialty length is bounded in practice by the container's request-line limit and is carried only as a bound query parameter and a URL-encoded link parameter; it composes no filesystem path, no resource lookup, and no deserialization input.

Exposed surface and supply chain: no new endpoint is added - both /vets.html and /vets gain an optional parameter on an already-public read route, and the JSON endpoint returns the same Vets projection as before, so no new field is exposed. build.gradle and gradle/ are untouched, so no dependency is added, removed, or repinned and the resolved dependency set is unchanged from the last verified state; the plain-HTTP repository check and TLS resolution are unaffected. Secret sweep over the added lines (password, secret, token, key, credential, and the specialty/filter vocabulary this change introduces) found no hardcoded value.

findings.description: Finding 1 (BDD naming) is fully resolved: all six renamed methods (theSpecialtySearchShouldFindEveryVeterinarianHoldingIt, theSpecialtySearchShouldMatchRegardlessOfLetterCase, theSpecialtySearchShouldNotMatchPartOfAStoredName, theSpecialtySearchShouldFindNoVeterinarianForAnUnheldSpecialty, theSpecialtySearchShouldPageOverTheMatchingVeterinariansAlone, theVetListNarrowedBySpecialtyShouldShowOnlyTheHoldersRegardlessOfLetterCase) now follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school and are consistent with the rest of the slice. Finding 2's new test theVetListShouldRenderNoControlForChoosingASpecialty is real, non-vacuous (verified by re-running the injected-form check myself: current vetList.html has zero <form>/<input>/<select> tags, confirming clean restoration), and does close most of the gap. However PAGE_WITH_A_SPECIALTY_CONTROL = "(?is).*<(?:form|input|select)\\b[^>]*specialty.*" requires the literal substring "specialty" inside the control tag's own opening-tag attributes ([^>]* cannot cross a >). A control that lets a caller choose a specialty but names its parameter/id something else -- e.g. <select name="filter"><option value="radiology">Radiology</option>...</select>, or a <label>Specialty</label><select id="s"> pairing -- is exactly the control shape acceptance criterion 11 forbids, yet it renders undetected because the word "specialty" never appears inside the select tag itself. The test proves 'no control literally labeled specialty' rather than the criterion's 'no control for choosing a specialty'.
findings.fix: Broaden the assertion beyond a literal attribute-name match, e.g. also assert the rendered page contains no <select>/<input> whose enclosed <option> values or list of values equal the known specialty names from the fixture data (radiology, surgery, dentistry), or match on the surrounding <label>/nearby text as well as the tag attributes -- so a differently-named specialty-choosing control still fails the test.
